title: runtime/scheduler: reduce lock contention with per-class queues (sharded locks + lock-free fast path)
author: Marcus Reed
description:
Context: After landing per-class queues for the mixed-workload scheduler prototype (short/long prompt split), we saw elevated scheduler CPU and intermittent queueing jitter under high concurrency. Profiling pointed to lock contention on the scheduler mutex during enqueue/dequeue + metric bookkeeping (queue depth, wait-time hist buckets). This PR reduces contention by (1) sharding locks per class queue, (2) moving a bunch of stats updates off the hot lock path, and (3) tightening critical sections so kernel dispatch selection doesn’t hold scheduler locks.

What changed (high level): - Replace global Scheduler::mu with per-queue locks (short_mu, long_mu) and a small global lock only for cross-queue state (fairness window bookkeeping + active batch bookkeeping). - Introduce a lock-free fast path for queue depth and wait-time sampling (atomic counters + sampled histogram enqueue) to avoid taking queue locks just to bump gauges. - Move trace span creation and label formatting out of the locked region; spans now capture timestamps at lock boundary and add attributes after release. - Refactor dequeue selection: choose candidate queue under minimal locking, then pop from that queue under its own lock; the fairness window state is updated after pop to avoid lock nesting. - Add a regression microbench that simulates 256 concurrent producers with mixed short/long arrivals and asserts scheduler thread time doesn’t regress beyond a bound.

Before/after results (A100, runtime perf lab, 2x scheduling threads, mixed trace replay 70/30 short/long, 350 rps steady-state; scheduler flag ON): - Scheduler thread CPU (combined): 92–98% -> 55–63% (pprof ‘scheduler_loop’ inclusive). - Mutex contention samples (perf lock): 14.7% -> 3.1% of samples in pthread_mutex_lock within scheduler. - Enqueue+classify median wall: 38 µs -> 16 µs; p99: 310 µs -> 92 µs. - Tail latency (end-to-end) improvement is mostly indirect (less jitter): p95 for short class improved ~4–7% depending on scenario; p99 improved ~6–10%. Throughput unchanged within noise (+0.3% mean tokens/s).

Profiling notes / evidence: - pprof capture: `RUNTIME_PPROF=1` (30s) during `bench/mixed_replay --scenario=dedicated_like_1 --concurrency=256` shows contention moving from `Scheduler::enqueue`/`Scheduler::dequeue` into expected work (tokenization + network). - perf record with `--call-graph dwarf` shows `pthread_mutex_lock` dropping substantially; remaining hot path is expected atomic increments + queue pop. - Flamegraphs and raw summaries attached in Linear (ENG-4823 comment) and linked from the benchmark lab run `benchlab://runs/2024-11-20-mixed-replay-8495`.

Risk / rollout: - Semantics should be unchanged; this is intended to be internal optimization only. - Still behind `scheduler.mixed_workload.enabled` flag. - Added a TSAN-only test in CI for queue lock ordering to catch accidental nesting; all locks are non-reentrant and we now enforce a single lock acquisition order (global -> queue) where needed.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests updated/added (scheduler fairness sim still passes). - [x] Microbench added for contention regression. - [x] pprof/perf evidence attached (see links in ENG-4823). - [x] No config changes; flag behavior unchanged.

Follow-ups (not in this PR): - Consider moving wait-time hist updates fully to a per-thread buffer to reduce atomic pressure (Omar’s suggestion). - Revisit tracing sampling rate for enqueue/dequeue spans; still a measurable cost at very high QPS (Julian tracking).

Notes for reviewers: The mechanical diff is bigger than the behavior change because I split Scheduler::State into Scheduler::GlobalState + QueueState. I tried to keep naming consistent with PRs 8444/8439. Most of the functional logic should look the same; the main intent is reducing time spent holding any lock during metric emission and routing decisions.
commits: runtime/scheduler: split global state from per-queue state
runtime/scheduler: shard locks per class queue and tighten critical sections
runtime/metrics: move queue depth + wait-time sampling off hot lock path
runtime/tracing: defer span attribute formatting until after lock release
bench: add scheduler lock contention microbench + regression bound
tests: add TSAN lock-order smoke test for scheduler queues
review_conversation: Sofia Ivanova: Can you confirm we never hold global + both queue locks at once? The fairness window update looks like it could accidentally nest if we refactor later. Also please add a comment about the lock acquisition order.

Marcus Reed (author): Confirmed. I added `LOCKING.md` style comments in scheduler.h: global_mu may be taken alone; queue_mu may be taken alone; if both are taken, order is global_mu -> queue_mu and never both queues. Added TSAN smoke test that intentionally exercises enqueue/dequeue paths and asserts no inversion under stress.

Omar El-Sayed: The atomic increments for hist buckets are still inside enqueue() right now. Can we sample 1/N and move heavy work out? Also please post before/after numbers for `enqueue()` p99 specifically; that’s what showed up in canary traces.

Marcus Reed (author): Added sampling gate (1/16 by default; same as other scheduler spans) so hist updates are cheap most of the time. Posted p50/p99 in the PR description and linked the benchlab run. Enqueue p99 dropped from ~310us to ~92us in the main mixed replay scenario.

Julian Moore: Please ensure trace spans don’t capture references to request objects after releasing the lock (lifetime). Also naming: metric `scheduler_queue_wait_ms` should keep same tags to not break dashboards.

Marcus Reed (author): Good catch. Switched span creation to copy IDs/timestamps only; no request refs. Metric tags unchanged (class=short|long, route, model). Verified dashboards in staging still render.
Hiro Tanaka: Any impact on kernel dispatch selection? We’ve had issues when scheduler changes accidentally alter batching shape or timing. Are we changing batching boundaries?

Marcus Reed (author): No change to batching decision logic; this is purely about locks around existing enqueue/dequeue and accounting. I verified batch size distribution histograms (prefill batch tokens, decode batch tokens) match baseline within noise in the same trace replay.
release_notes: None (internal perf optimization behind existing mixed-workload scheduler flag).
